group_assessment.weighting: FOUR-AUTHOR EDITORIAL AND THE WEIGHTING IS NOT THE SAME FOR ALL FOUR. Nan-Shan Chang (corresponding, and the author of the WOX1/Tau/Zfra line), Rongtuan Lin, Chun-I Sze and Rami Aqeilan. Measured 2026-09-09: 'Aqeilan RI[Author]' = 137 PubMed records, 64 with WWOX in title/abstract. The document is primary for NOTHING - it reports no experiment - and its statements are of three kinds, each weighted differently in this reading: (a) summaries of Research Topic articles, which are pointers and carry the weight of the article pointed at; (b) claims about the literature attributed to numbered references, carried only as far as the reference identity; (c) ONE clinical claim sourced to an unpublished personal communication, which is carried as a lead and not as evidence. The corresponding author's own therapeutic programme (Zfra, Ser14) is summarised by himself here, so it is a self-summary and adds no independent weight.

multihop.note: THE CITATION STRUCTURE OF THIS DOCUMENT IS ITSELF A FINDING. The deposit carries SIX numbered references, each with its PMID in an ext-link-type='pmid' element, while the body cites TEN distinct Research Topic articles by author name through URI ext-links to doi.org, with no reference-list entry and no PMID. Both blind auditors recounted and agreed: 6 ref elements, 10 distinct Research Topic articles (Chen et al. linked five times), 0 fig, 0 table-wrap, 0 graphic, abstract absent entirely. An enumeration trusting the ref-element count alone would report six and miss ten gene-direct pointers. 🔴 AND THE DEPOSIT CARRIED THE NUMBERED REFERENCES' PMIDs ALL ALONG: this reader resolved them by external author search instead of reading the markup, and got one of the six wrong. The identifiers were inside the artefact. Of the nine sources resolved, TWO are read in this corpus - 30370248 (complete) and 30158849 (partial), both Research Topic articles resolved externally from their DOIs - and SEVEN have no receipt of any kind.

entries.proposition: 🔴 THE HEADLINE OF THIS READING, AND ITS EVIDENTIARY STATUS IS THE WEAKEST POSSIBLE. An editorial with no data of its own carries a CLINICAL-TREATMENT statement about the exact intervention class this repository has rejected in DIS-003 - and sources it to an unpublished personal communication. There is no genotype, no n, no design, no seizure outcome measure, no transcript or protein readout, and the population is 'patients with neurodegeneration', which is not stated to be WWOX-DEE newborns. It is recorded as a LEAD WITH NAMED PROVENANCE and explicitly NOT as evidence.
entries.snippet: Preliminary findings from clinical treatment shows that despite mutations, forced transcription of WWOX gene appears to be a feasible approach to lessen the symptoms of seizure in patients with neurodegeneration (personal communications with Dr. D. S. Lin at the Taipei Medical University)
entries.anchor: Concluding section, 'what's urgent for the field' paragraph

entries.proposition: The unmet need the editorial names, in the authors' own terms, and the endpoint it names for it. AUDIT-CORRECTED: the original said the two sentences sit 'two lines apart'; both auditors checked and they are DIRECTLY ADJACENT in the same paragraph. Adjacency is the stronger form of the point - the clinical claim of entry 0 follows immediately on the statement of the need it claims to have met.
entries.snippet: an effective drug to lessen seizure in the newborn patients would greatly benefit them
entries.anchor: Concluding section, 'what's urgent for the field' paragraph

entries.proposition: A MOLECULE PROPOSED FOR WWOX-DEFICIENCY NEURAL DISEASE BY NAME. Zfra is already carried in this corpus's therapeutic hypotheses and discovery ledgers, so this is not a new lead; what the editorial adds is that the primary group proposes it specifically for neural disease associated with WWOX deficiency, in a sentence with no data behind it in this document.
entries.snippet: Zfra peptides can be used as therapeutic options and strategies to target cancer and neural diseases associated with WWOX deficiency

entries.proposition: The mechanism claimed for Zfra, attributed to refs 4 and 5. Reference identity verified AGAINST THE DEPOSIT'S OWN MARKUP: ref 4 = Lee 2017, Alzheimers Dement 3:189-204, pmid ext-link 29067327; ref 5 = Lee 2015, Oncotarget 6:3737-51, pmid ext-link 25686832. Neither carries a receipt in this corpus - a statement about the ledger, not about this artefact, and marked as such. The endpoints are MURINE: cancer growth and memory loss in mice, not seizures and not human.
entries.snippet: Suppression of Ser14 phosphorylation by a zinc finger peptide Zfra blocks cancer growth and restores memory loss in mice

entries.proposition: 🔴 THIS SOURCE NAMES TWO WWOX PHOSPHORYLATION SITES AND GIVES THEM OPPOSITE FUNCTIONAL CONSEQUENCES - Tyr33 for anticancer response, Ser14 for disease progression. AUDIT-CORRECTED, and the correction is a scoping one: the original proposition spent most of its length asserting facts about a DIFFERENT paper (PMID 26499798's Figure 2A, four measured residue positions, and the withdrawal of an identification under blind audit). Both auditors flagged that those facts are absent from this artefact - grep confirms zero occurrences of 287, 33.2, 286.9, 12.3 or 14.3 here - and one graded the triple OVERSHOOT for it. WHAT THIS LOCATOR NOW CARRIES IS ONLY WHAT THIS DOCUMENT SAYS. The cross-paper reconciliation is a two-artefact statement and lives in the dossier and the commit candidate, where both artefacts are named and fingerprinted.
entries.snippet: switch of the phosphorylation of WWOX at Tyr33 for anticancer response to Ser14 for disease progression
entries.anchor: Research Topic articles, Liu et al. paragraph

The editorial reports the locus as one of five new risk factors; this reading does not verify that against the GWAS itself and does not carry it as a datum.

entries.proposition: The family-level denominator the editorial gives for WW domain proteins, attributed to ref 1 = Huang and Chang 2018, Exp Biol Med 243:137-47. 🔴 AUDIT-CORRECTED, AND THIS WAS A FACTUAL ERROR OF MINE: the original gave ref 1 as PMID 29581896. THE DEPOSIT ITSELF CARRIES THE PMID in its reference markup - ext-link-type='pmid' 29310447 - and 29581896 is a different Chang-group paper (FRET microscopy, Cell Death Discov 2018). Both auditors checked the deposit and both were right. The method failure is the point: I ran an external author search and took its first hit, when the identifier was inside the artefact I already had open. 29310447 has NO RECEIPT in this corpus, and it is the reference that would settle what the other paper of this wave marks and does not name.

entries.proposition: 🔴 ADDED AFTER THE BLIND AUDIT: BOTH AUDITORS INDEPENDENTLY NAMED THIS SENTENCE AS UNCOVERED, AND THEY WERE RIGHT. It is a SECOND forward-looking clinical claim, structurally weaker than the one at entry 0: that one at least names an unpublished source, while this one carries NO attribution at all - no reference, no personal communication, nothing - and asserts a preventive effect on Alzheimer's disease in middle-aged individuals with the modal 'would likely'. The finding of this reading is therefore not 'the editorial contains one unsupported clinical claim' but that it contains TWO, adjacent, and the weaker of them is the one with no source. An audit that only checks the propositions written is not an audit; the omission was the finding.
entries.snippet: Furthermore, blocking the downregulation of WWOX in the middle aged individuals would likely to prevent the development of AD

Carried as a POINTER with the weight of the article pointed at, which in this case is a paper already read here at full depth.

verbatim_locators.audit_note: R4 SATISFIED, run AFTER the reading was landed and BEFORE any commit candidate - the order chosen deliberately because a session rate limit had already killed the first two auditors mid-run, and a landed reading with no commit candidate touches no claim. TWO independent blind auditors, 17 triples each, given only the triples, the artefact and the canonical text of CLAIM 023 and DIS-003. Result: ZERO NOT_IN_SOURCE quotes - every quote is a verbatim substring of the deposit. ONE FACTUAL ERROR, caught by both: entry 6 gave ref 1's PMID as 29581896 where the deposit's own markup says 29310447, and 29581896 is a different paper entirely. ONE SCOPING OVERSHOOT, caught by both: entry 4 asserted facts about a different paper that are absent from this artefact, and has been narrowed to what this document says. Three smaller corrections taken (entries 1, 10, 11, 15) on adjacency and on the provenance of externally resolved identifiers. 🔴 THE MOST VALUABLE FINDING OF THIS AUDIT WAS AN OMISSION, NOT AN ERROR, AND BOTH AUDITORS FOUND IT INDEPENDENTLY: no triple covered 'Furthermore, blocking the downregulation of WWOX in the middle aged individuals would likely to prevent the development of AD' - a SECOND forward-looking clinical claim, adjacent to the one this reading was built on and WEAKER, because it carries no attribution at all where the first at least names a personal communication. Three locators were added on the auditors' omission list (entries 17, 18, 19), and the reading's headline changed shape: the document contains two unsupported clinical claims, not one. The auditors did not disagree with each other on any verdict in this paper.
